blob_features — BLOB measure op

• Data kinds: labels2d → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.blob_features(labels: 'Any', spacing: 'float' = 1.0) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import blob2d; blob2d.blob_features(labels: 'Any', spacing: 'float' = 1.0) -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsblob.get("blob_features"))

Usage

Returns the shape features of each object as 1 array per key.

Parameters

labels : array_like

Output of blob_label (integers, background 0).

spacing : float

Size of 1 pixel [unit/px]. Lengths are multiplied by it, areas by its 2nd power.

Default 1.0 = stays in pixels.

Returns

dict

n (number of objects), spacing, units (mapping item → unit), and

19 arrays of length n (FEATURE_KEYS). Even with 0 objects,

all keys are present with empty arrays (so the caller need not branch).

Notes

• angle is the tilt in the matrix coordinate system (+column → +row is positive = clockwise on screen).

• major / minor are the axis lengths of the ellipse with the same 2nd-order moments (4 sqrt(lambda)). It is not the bounding extent of the pixel arrangement, so for a square it comes out slightly longer than the side -- this is as defined, not an error.

• circularity is 4 pi A / P^2. HALCON's circularity is "area / area of the circle whose radius is the farthest point", a different thing, so when comparing values, check the definition.

• Objects with touches_border True have both area and perimeter smaller by the cut-off part. Discard them before counting, or count the ground-truth side by the same convention.

Examples

>>> import numpy as np

>>> m = np.zeros((20, 20), bool); m[4:14, 4:9] = True

>>> f = blob_features(blob_label(m))

>>> int(f["n"]), float(f["area"][0])

(1, 50.0)
